Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

solution noun

a way out of a difficulty

also find a solution, no solution, way out, answer (to a problem), resolution (of a problem), resolve (a problem)

classical

Ter. Ph. 616: invēnī, opīnor, remedium huic reī
Ter. And. 468: quod remedium nunc huic malō inveniam?

remedium, remediī n.

noun, second declension

a remedy, a solution (to a problem)

Terence’s word whenever a slave or a son needs a way out, with the dative of the trouble (huic reī, huic malō). Also a medicine or cure (see remedy).

Other words

  • exitus, exitūs m. — a way out

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 22.12: numquam exitum inveniēs; Cic. Att. 10.14.1: nūllīus cōnsilī exitum invēnimus

    To find a way of doing something: ratiōnem invenīre (see approach, a way of dealing with something).

  • solūtiō, solūtiōnis f. — the solution (of a practical problem)

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · Traupman 185: Quae igitur est solūtiō?; Traupman 382

    Classically the solving of a puzzle or an argument (see solution, the answer to a puzzle); Traupman uses it of a practical problem.

Examples

  • Invēnī, opīnor, remedium huic reī. — Quid, Geta? — Quod remedium?

    I think I’ve found a way out of this. — What is it, Geta? — What way out?Ter. Ph. 616–617

  • Quod remedium nunc huic malō inveniam?

    What way out can I find from this trouble now?Ter. And. 468

  • numquam exitum inveniēs. Nēmō cum sarcinīs ēnatat.

    You will never find a way out. Nobody swims to safety with his luggage.Sen. Ep. 22.12

  • Cuivīs dolōrī remedium est patientia.

    For any pain, the remedy is patience.Publil. Sent. C 12

See also problem, solution, approach, remedy.
